title: Matched-volume-fraction comparison of exogenous chitin and basalt reinforcement in SCOBY-derived cellulose matrices
scope: Compare characterized shrimp-derived chitin-containing reinforcement and basalt reinforcement in matched SCOBY-derived cellulose matrices using matched filler volume fraction and a common matrix-processing baseline. This record is a comparative research framework, not a claim that either filler is superior before measurement.
application_boundary: No material is assigned a skin, wearable, structural, food, medical, or other application class by this comparison record.

core_hypothesis.claim: Shrimp-derived chitin-containing reinforcement and basalt reinforcement may produce different composition-structure-property trade-offs in a SCOBY cellulose matrix; the direction and magnitude of these effects are unverified.

comparison_principle.rule: Mass fraction alone is insufficient because chitin-containing materials and basalt have different densities. Comparisons intended to isolate reinforcement efficiency must use matched filler volume fraction or explicitly report the conversion and resulting volume fractions.

BASELINE_GEN1.note: Used to distinguish reinforcement effects from tension-drying/process effects.

experimental_matrix.replication: At least three independent specimens or batches per condition for exploratory comparison; stronger inference requires an adequately powered design.
experimental_matrix.randomization: Specimen cutting and measurement order should be randomized or blocked to reduce position and operator effects.
experimental_matrix.blinding: Where practical, specimen identifiers should conceal reinforcement type during mechanical testing and primary image scoring.

normalized_metrics.volume_fraction_rule: All cross-filler comparisons must use measured or traceably calculated filler volume fraction.
normalized_metrics.uncertainty: Report measurement uncertainty and replicate dispersion for all headline comparisons.

statistical_gate.primary_comparison: Compare each reinforcement condition against GEN1 and matched-volume-fraction chitin versus basalt conditions.
statistical_gate.multiple_comparison_control: Pre-specify an appropriate multiplicity correction or omnibus model before confirmatory interpretation.
statistical_gate.effect_size: Report effect sizes and confidence intervals, not p-values alone.
statistical_gate.warning: n=3 is exploratory and may be underpowered; non-significance must not be interpreted as proof of equivalence.

decision_logic.if_strength_increases_but_wet_retention_: Record as dry-strength improvement only; do not claim overall reinforcement superiority.
decision_logic.if_modulus_increases_but_toughness_or_el: Record as stiffness gain with possible embrittlement trade-off.
decision_logic.if_chitin_outperforms_basalt_at_matched_: Hypothesis partially supported for the tested property set only; investigate structure and interface before generalization.
decision_logic.if_basalt_outperforms_chitin: Hypothesis partially supported for the tested property set only; do not generalize to all basalt or chitin forms.
decision_logic.if_no_difference_is_detected: Retain uncertainty; investigate statistical power, dispersion, filler morphology and interface before concluding equivalence.
decision_logic.if_density_normalized_advantage_reverses: Report both absolute and specific metrics and preserve the trade-off rather than selecting a preferred metric post hoc.

claim_corrections: Intrinsic filler modulus is not the same as composite modulus or strength.
Continuous basalt-fiber properties cannot be transferred directly to short fibers, powder, or low-loading inclusions.
Chitin nanofibril properties cannot be transferred directly to coarse shrimp-shell powder.
A lower density does not automatically imply higher specific strength in the final composite.
Improved mechanical properties may arise from densification, drying, interfacial changes, or other processing artifacts rather than the reinforcement phase itself.
Matched mass fraction is not an adequate cross-material comparison when filler densities differ.

safety_boundary.shellfish_allergen: Crustacean-derived material can contain residual allergenic proteins; handling and any intended human-contact use require appropriate contamination and residue controls.
safety_boundary.mineral_fiber: Basalt fibers or fines can generate respirable particulate; handling requires appropriate dust controls and PPE.
safety_boundary.unknown_composite: Mechanical testing and downstream handling should not imply food, medical, or inhalation safety.
safety_boundary.food_boundary: No food-contact or ingestion claim is admitted.

next_gate: FREEZE_REINFORCEMENT_MATERIAL_SPECIFICATIONS_AND_SELECTED_VOLUME_FRACTION_LEVELS; PREPARE_MATCHED_CHITIN_AND_BASALT_CONDITIONS WITH COMMON SCOBY MATRIX AND PROCESS HISTORY; CHARACTERIZE DISTRIBUTION AND INTERFACE; THEN EXECUTE BLINDED MECHANICAL/WET TESTING AND REPORT ABSOLUTE AND DENSITY-NORMALIZED METRICS.
authority_rule: This record is a preregistered comparison framework. It does not establish that chitin or basalt is superior, and it does not promote either material to an application class without measured evidence.
